name: crash-cut-transcripts
description: Every commit path's media operations in their normative order, and the states a reboot after a cut before, during or after any of them may produce. A cut is enumerated at three positions per operation: before it reaches the card, during it (a write tears the program page it was programming; a sync commits an arbitrary subset), and after it returns.

transcripts.name: journal-append
transcripts.description: One journal record. Journal slots are the single exemption from the invalidate-first discipline, so the body write carries the zeroed gate sector itself.

steps.note: the whole stride: body, a zeroed gate sector, and a zeroed pad
the body is durable and the slot carries no valid gate
the gate that makes the body a record
the commit point

transcripts.name: checkpoint-compaction
transcripts.description: Compaction writes and gates the inactive checkpoint completely before the new epoch's first record exists.
transcripts.note: PROVISIONAL, in one respect only: the body appears here as a single 65,024-byte write because that is what the reference implementation does. Section 6.3 specifies a bounded forward pass, region by region and entry by entry, staging at most one 208-byte entry plus a 512-byte sector — so a conforming writer emits many writes here, not one. The ordering around it is normative and is what the cut points test: invalidate the inactive gate, sync; write the whole body, sync; write the gate, sync; only then the first record of the new epoch. The streaming pass lands with the compaction engine and will replace this step's shape.

the inactive checkpoint is now unusable and its body may be reused
the complete body at epoch E + 1 and through-sequence S

the O2CG gate
the new checkpoint is selected and every old-epoch slot is inert
only now, sequence S + 1 at slot zero of epoch E + 1
its body
its gate
the first commit of the new epoch

admissibleOutcomes: the old checkpoint plus its old-epoch journal suffix
the new checkpoint alone, which is the same catalog at epoch E + 1
the new checkpoint plus the first record of the new epoch

transcripts.name: ride-checkpoint
transcripts.description: One ride checkpoint: payload first, then the ring slot at sequence mod 16.
transcripts.note: A ride payload is smaller than one 16,384-byte program page, so a cut during its write tears the whole file and the ride restarts at zero. Section 1.1 caps that at one checkpoint interval and calls it not a store fault. Whatever recovery resumes from, the durable bytes must back its finalized prefix CRC.

the new checkpoint is authoritative

admissibleOutcomes: the initial durable offset zero, when the cut tore the payload page itself

transcripts.name: short-write
transcripts.description: A write the medium truncates. The writer checks the returned length and abandons the commit.
transcripts.note: One step, because the sequence stops there: the length check fails and nothing after it runs. There are no cut points to enumerate — the fault is the write's own return value.

steps.note: the body stride, of which the medium accepts fewer bytes

admissibleOutcomes: the projection before the record; a short write is an error, never a success

transcripts.name: media-full
transcripts.description: A write the medium refuses for want of space.
transcripts.note: One step, for the same reason as the short write: the refusal ends the sequence.

steps.note: the body stride, which the medium refuses outright

transcripts.name: corrupt-read
transcripts.description: An ordinary commit, followed by a mount whose reads are poisoned one at a time.
transcripts.note: The fault here is on the read path, not the write path, so the steps are an ordinary append and the injection happens during recovery. A corrupt read can cost visibility; it can never invent state.

steps.note: an ordinary append, completed before the fault
its body
its gate
the commit point; the fault is injected into a later *read*

admissibleOutcomes: no checkpoint at all, when the poisoned read was the only valid checkpoint's
